questions.prompt: A packet's destination is on a network attached to one of the router's own interfaces. What does the router do?
options: Looks for a static route first
Sends it to the default route
Delivers it directly on that local network

questions.prompt: Put these in the order the basic algorithm tries them.
options: Routing table, local network, static route, default route
Local network, static route, routing table, default route
Default route, routing table, static route, local network
Static route, local network, default route, routing table

questions.prompt: Write the default route in CIDR notation.
A static route automatically switches to a backup path when its link fails.
Why do most networks block source-routed packets?
options: The sender chooses the path, so an attacker can steer traffic around firewalls

questions.prompt: What's another name for the router a host sends everything to when it has no better route? (two words)
Routes learned from other routers by a routing protocol are called dynamic routes.
A small office has exactly one connection, to its ISP. What's the simplest sensible routing setup for its router?
options: A static default route pointing at the ISP
